name: Annamacharya Nitya Annadanam Trust (Ahobila Mutt)
why_it_matters: The free-meal trust run by Sri Ahobila Matam for devotees of Sri Lakshmi Narasimha — the central pilgrim meal in a remote shrine town. Prasadam is offered three times a day: dadiyannam (curd rice) morning and evening, and tadiyaradhanam (a full-course meal) at noon. The Ahobila Mutt has managed Ahobilam's nine Narasimha shrines for centuries.
insider_tip: The noon tadiyaradhanam is the full meal — time your morning of shrine-visiting to be back at Lower Ahobilam by lunch. Free of charge; donations to the trust are welcomed. The Mutt also runs the choultry accommodation.

name: Brahmana Nitya Annadana Satram
why_it_matters: A free-meal satram in Upper Ahobilam — the temple cluster 8km up a narrow forested valley from Lower Ahobilam — feeding nearly 400 pilgrims daily. With effectively no restaurants in Upper Ahobilam, this is the meal for anyone doing the harder upper-shrine trek, where the Ugra Narasimha cave temple sits.
insider_tip: Go around 12.30-1.30pm — that is when the food is fresh, hot and reliably available. Free, with donations welcomed. Carry water for the upper-shrine walk; there is little else along the valley.
signature_address: Brahmana Nitya Annadana Satram, Upper Ahobilam 518543

name: APTDC Haritha Hotel Restaurant
area: Lower Ahobilam, near Prahladavarada Narasimha Temple
signature_dish: Vegetarian meals and South Indian tiffin
why_it_matters: The restaurant inside the small AP Tourism (APTDC Haritha) hotel at Lower Ahobilam, near the Prahladavarada Narasimha Temple — an 8-room property and the only real served-meal option for non-pilgrim-routine visitors. Vegetarian breakfast, lunch and dinner; the cook will prepare something on request given enough notice.
insider_tip: It is a tiny hotel — if you want a specific dish or a meal outside standard hours, ask the cook in advance. Pre-order is wise as the kitchen cooks to demand. The most reliable non-annadanam meal in town.

name: Lower Ahobilam Village Tiffin Stalls
why_it_matters: The small cluster of basic eateries in Lower Ahobilam village serving South Indian staples — idli, dosa and simple thalis — for pilgrims outside annadanam hours. In a town this remote, in the Nallamala forest, these stalls are the practical quick-eat between shrine visits; honest pilgrim-village food, not destination dining.
insider_tip: Stick to freshly cooked idli, dosa and hot tea. Hours are loose and tied to the temple footfall — eat when food is being cooked rather than expecting all-day service. Cash; carry small notes.
signature_address: Lower Ahobilam village main road, Lower Ahobilam 518543
